name: Twisted cube
status: new as far as the sources checked go: member A's h-tile (lambda = 3/8), convex, 6 squares and 6 triangles; not found in the sources checked (#86 Section 8: library and web searches, Grünbaum–Shephard 1980, Gabbrielli–Jiao–Torquato 2012, Fedorov 1885, Lalvani 1990); #86 claims nothing as new until Goldberg's lists of space-filling polyhedra are read; its c-tile partner, the brick of two cubes, is classical
scale_note: frame: the close-packed layers at ball spacing sqrt2 in orthonormal rational coordinates (layers perpendicular to (1, 1, 1): in-layer lattice a1 = (1, -1, 0), a2 = (1, 0, -1), one layer = (2/3)(1, 1, 1); the frame of Chucky and Fang); the papers' values are at ball spacing 1: divide lengths by sqrt2 and volumes by 2 sqrt2 (so the volume 2 here is one layer cell, 1/sqrt2). The layer's ball is at the origin. Pieces: tiles.py of #75 (census engine of #53/#57, unchanged), weights w_oct = 0, w_tet = lambda; tile h of layer 0 of AB (h) at lambda = 3/8, the Rule of Halves split (#57): the top half of the octahedral piece below, the two tetrahedral pieces, the bottom half of the octahedral piece above; in-layer lattice shifts per piece (tiles.py order) [[0, 0], [0, 0]] (#86 pairs.json, member A); joined exactly by exactfaces.union_faces (coplanar faces merged; a corner of one face lying inside a side of the next face is a corner of both, so faces may list such straight corners).

centre.kind: corner centroid (mean of the corners; the frame origin is not the centre)

unit_volume.note: x -> centre + s (x - centre), s = V^(-1/3) with V the exact volume above; s is symbolic and the corners are decimals (15 places, as elsewhere). Same corner order and faces as above; volume 1.
